content: Substances in your diet can influence how medications work. Children may exhibit heightened sensitivity to the side effects of this drug. Older adults are also more likely to experience side effects, particularly drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. It is known to pass into breast milk and may cause undesirable effects in a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. It is important to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels of all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as allergy skin tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Symptoms of overdose may include severe drowsiness, seizures, or dilated pupils. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from moisture and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Liquid forms of this medication should not be frozen. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine used to relieve symptoms of allergies, hay fever, and the common cold. These symptoms include rash, itching, watery eyes, itchy eyes/nose/throat, cough, runny nose, and sneezing. It is also used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness. This medication works by blocking histamine, a natural substance your body produces during an allergic reaction. Cough-and-cold products have not been proven safe or effective in children under 6 years of age. Do not use this product to treat cold symptoms in children younger than 6 years unless specifically directed by a doctor. Certain products, such as long-acting tablets or capsules, are not recommended for children under 12 years. These products do not cure or shorten the duration of the common cold and may cause serious side effects. To minimize the risk of serious side effects, follow all dosage instructions carefully. Do not use this product to make a child sleepy. Avoid giving other cough-and-cold medications that may contain the same or similar ingredients. Follow all directions on the product package. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, take it as directed. Take the tablet, capsule, or liquid form by mouth with or without food. Use a special measuring device or spoon for liquid forms to ensure the correct dose; do not use a household spoon. Rapidly-dissolving tablets or strips should be allowed to dissolve on the tongue and then swallowed, with or without water. Dosage is based on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. There are many brands and forms of diphenhydramine available, so read the dosing instructions carefully for each product, as the amount of diphenhydramine may vary. To prevent motion sickness, take your dose 30 minutes before starting activities such as travel. To help you sleep, take your dose about 30 minutes before bedtime. Common side effects may include drowsiness, dizziness, constipation, stomach upset, blurred vision, or dry mouth/nose/throat. If your doctor has directed you to use this medication, remember that they have judged the benefit to you to outweigh the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking diphenhydramine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to dimenhydrinate, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Do not drive, use machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages. Liquid products, chewable tablets, or dissolving tablets/strips may contain sugar and/or aspartame. Liquid products may also contain alcohol. Exercise caution if you have diabetes, liver disease, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any other condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug. Older adults may also be more sensitive, particularly to drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant.
